title: Accumulation is selective. Earnings and cash flow must carry the next leg.
thesis: The useful question is whether institutional persistence is accompanied by improving economics at a defensible price. This issue follows four contrasting situations: cash-backed expansion, bank growth with a funding constraint, an exchange whose operating momentum exceeds its fund-ownership momentum, and disagreement between domestic and foreign ownership measures. These are selected research cases, not a forecast for the entire Indian market.

cases.title: Accumulation has a cash-flow cross-check
cases.facts: Acutaas reported consolidated H1 FY27 operating cash flow of ₹215.92 crore and total PAT of ₹198.14 crore. Property, plant and equipment purchases were ₹123.92 crore. Q2 revenue was ₹436.92 crore and total PAT ₹123.14 crore. These are reported results, not forecasts.
cases.calculation: Operating cash flow / total PAT = 215.919 / 198.1352 = 109.0%. Operating cash flow less PPE purchases = ₹92.00 crore; this narrow cash-surplus measure excludes other investing flows. Q1 revenue inferred as H1 minus Q2 was ₹329.67 crore, making Q2 growth 32.5% sequentially.
cases.interpretation: Cash generation adds substance to the accumulation signal. Nevertheless, a strong quarter can reflect product mix or shipment timing. The useful next question is whether demand and cash conversion persist as capacity grows.
cases.alternative: A manager may have increased shares after inflows or to rebalance a portfolio. The holdings cannot establish that the manager anticipated these results. Full-year returns on capital and a dated valuation still need to justify the entry price.

scenarios.label: Strengthens
scenarios.text: Subsequent results sustain revenue and margins, with operating cash flow covering expansion and inventories remaining controlled.

scenarios.label: Working case
scenarios.text: Growth continues but quarterly margins vary. Track cash conversion through the next half-year rather than extrapolating Q2.

scenarios.label: Weakens
scenarios.text: Inventory or receivables absorb cash while margins fall; repeated additions alone would no longer offer a persuasive cross-check.

cases.checkpoint: Next quarterly revenue and margin; next half-year operating cash flow versus PAT and PPE spending.

sources.label: NSE: Acutaas consolidated Q2 and H1 FY27 results, approved 27 Oct 2026

cases.title: The growth story has a funding test
cases.facts: City Union Bank's September 2026 presentation reports advances of ₹72,441.5 crore, deposits of ₹83,893.1 crore and CASA deposits of ₹22,350.2 crore. Year-on-year advances grew 26%, deposits 21%, and CASA 14%. Q2 net profit was ₹415.9 crore, NIM 3.87%, gross NPA 1.44% and net NPA 0.48%.
cases.calculation: Advances / deposits = 86.4%, versus 82.8% a year earlier using the disclosed balances. CASA / deposits = 26.6%, versus 28.1%. Q2 non-tax provisions rose from ₹57 crore to ₹120 crore; the ₹245 crore total provision line includes ₹125 crore of tax and should not all be treated as credit cost.
cases.interpretation: Loan expansion is running ahead of funding growth. A lower low-cost deposit share can raise funding pressure even when headline profit is strong. Institutional additions are more convincing if the bank preserves margins and underwriting while funding this expansion.
cases.alternative: Higher provisions are not by themselves proof of loan deterioration; their composition and subsequent slippages matter. Share additions and a falling foreign ownership percentage also have different denominators and reporting windows.

scenarios.label: Strengthens
scenarios.text: Deposit and CASA growth catch up with advances while margins and asset quality remain resilient.

scenarios.label: Working case
scenarios.text: Growth stays healthy but funding becomes more expensive. Earnings depend on managing the spread between loan yields and funding cost.

scenarios.label: Weakens
scenarios.text: Deposit competition compresses NIM at the same time as slippages and credit provisions rise.

cases.checkpoint: Next-quarter advances/deposits, CASA share, NIM and the non-tax provision breakdown. Check valuation against sustainable ROE and book value before considering an entry.

sources.label: City Union Bank: September 2026 investor presentation, pages 9–11

cases.title: Strong operations do not remove expectation risk
cases.facts: MCX's 4 November presentation reports H1 FY27 operating revenue of ₹1,502 crore and PAT of ₹868 crore, up 100.8% and 116.4% year on year. Options premium average daily turnover rose from ₹9,086 crore in Q1 to ₹10,291 crore in Q2. Its IR page displayed a delayed market capitalisation of ₹91,867.19 crore on 11 November 2026 at 14:13.
cases.calculation: Options premium turnover grew 13.3% sequentially. Market capitalisation / (2 × H1 PAT) is approximately 52.9 times. This is an illustrative annualised run-rate multiple, not a trailing P/E or an earnings forecast; it assumes the second half repeats the first.
cases.interpretation: The operating engine has momentum, yet the reconciled fund total shrank over the three-month window. The tension matters: a rapidly growing business can still disappoint if its valuation requires exceptional activity to persist. Share counts do not establish whether reductions reflected valuation discipline, redemptions or rebalancing.
cases.alternative: Trading activity can be cyclical, and revenue depends on product mix and monetisation. Notional options turnover is not exchange revenue. The November results were published after the October holdings date, so they cannot prove the reason for earlier fund decisions.

scenarios.label: Strengthens
scenarios.text: Options premium activity, active participation and revenue keep growing without meaningful margin deterioration.

scenarios.label: Working case
scenarios.text: Growth remains positive but moderates against a stronger base; the valuation leaves less room for operational disappointment.

scenarios.label: Weakens
scenarios.text: Activity normalises or regulation/competition changes monetisation, putting both earnings expectations and the valuation multiple under pressure.

cases.checkpoint: Monthly trading statistics, especially options premium turnover; next-quarter operating revenue and margin. Recalculate valuation with a fresh quote and complete trailing earnings.

sources.label: MCX: Q2/H1 FY27 investor presentation, 4 Nov 2026
MCX investor relations: dated market capitalisation and quote

cases.title: Opposing ownership signals deserve an open conclusion
cases.facts: The matched fund archive shows repeated reductions in Radico Khaitan. The saved FII/FPI series reports 18.20% in June and 19.43% in September 2026, a rise of 1.23 percentage points. This is a provider-sourced ownership series, last checked 22 October, and has not been newly reconciled to the original shareholding filings in this review.
cases.calculation: The FII change covers June–September; the mutual fund quantity comparison covers August–October. Those windows overlap only partly. Percentage ownership may also change with issued capital. The two measures cannot establish who traded with whom or prove that one investor group was better informed.
cases.interpretation: This belongs on a disagreement watchlist rather than a simple accumulation or distribution list. A useful investment conclusion requires business results, price paid and a common-period ownership comparison. We have withheld an earnings or valuation verdict here because those checks are not complete.
cases.alternative: Different mandates, reporting dates, position sizes and denominator changes can create the divergence. Foreign ownership is an aggregate category, not a single investment decision.

scenarios.label: Strengthens
scenarios.text: Fresh issuer results support earnings and cash generation, and subsequent comparable disclosures show broader ownership support.

scenarios.label: Working case
scenarios.text: Investor groups remain divided while the operating trend is unresolved; follow the evidence without assigning a directional trade call.

scenarios.label: Weakens
scenarios.text: Operating evidence deteriorates and reductions broaden across independently checked, comparable periods.

cases.checkpoint: Reconcile September and December statutory shareholding patterns and review the latest issuer results before treating this as a contrarian opportunity.

valuationRule: No buy/sell ranking or target price is assigned. A holding trend identifies a research lead; valuation must be checked with a dated price and an appropriate earnings or book-value denominator. The MCX run-rate sensitivity is explicitly illustrative.
scenarioRule: Scenarios are conditional interpretations for the next one to two reporting cycles. No probabilities or promised returns are assigned. Corporate evidence is reviewed as of 12 November 2026 and is not automatically refreshed when holdings change.
